newsitem.title: USA: Uncle B's 6-month net in line with goals.
newsitem.headline: Uncle B's 6-month net in line with goals.

text.p: Uncle Bo's Bakery Inc said on Thursday its results for the first six months of fiscal 1997 were in line with its annual goals.

Uncle B's, which makes bagels, earned $283,324 or $0.08 a share in the six months ended January 31, compared with a year-ago loss of $287,547 or $0.08 a share before a $0.40 charge for accounting changes. Its second quarter earnings were $15,330, compared with a year-ago loss of $437,740 or $0.12 a share.

"We are pleased with the most recent six months ended January 31, 1997, which set a record for the company in both revenue and earnings, and the results are in line with our annual goals," William Rose Jr., chairman, said in a statement.
Rose said sales and production efficiencies in the second quarter were hurt by about seven days of downtime due to the installation of new equipment and severe winter weather in January.

The completion of the next phase of the plant expansion may require some more downtime, but the project is expected to be completed by the end of the fourth quarter, he said. The expansion will allow Uncle B's to maintain income and sales momentum in future quarters, he added.
